title: Frente a: contrastar dos modelos o posiciones

sections.content: Frente a (as opposed to, in contrast with, facing) sets up an explicit contrast between two models, positions, or forces -- very useful when a reading needs to compare an old approach with a new one. It's followed by a noun phrase. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Frente a este modelo, las reformas neoliberales propusieron una lógica radicalmente distinta.
items.english: In contrast with this model, the neoliberal reforms proposed a radically different logic.

items.spanish: Muchos países otorgaron mayor independencia a sus bancos centrales frente al poder ejecutivo.
items.english: Many countries granted their central banks greater independence from the executive branch.

items.spanish: Frente a la desconfianza tradicional hacia el capital extranjero, los gobiernos comenzaron a atraer inversión activamente.
items.english: In contrast with the traditional distrust of foreign capital, governments began actively attracting investment.

items.spanish: Este cambio de paradigma, frente al modelo estatista de las décadas anteriores, no fue uniforme en ningún país.
items.english: This paradigm shift, as opposed to the statist model of previous decades, wasn't uniform in any country.

sections.content: Frente a can mean facing (physically or figuratively) or as opposed to (in contrast) depending on context -- when comparing two systems or eras, it almost always signals the contrastive sense.
